summary_html: The wider candidate s2_w160 passed every internal ship criterion (macro-F1 +0.060 on seen languages and +0.058 on never-seen languages, mean of 3 seeds, every role up), but it is not shipped: on the only external labelled data (Bouhoula et al., USENIX Security 2024: 2,204 real, mostly English cookie-banner button strings) its Reject F1 fell from 0.513 to 0.415 (precision 0.51 to 0.32), and in the app's layered decision it would emit 134 wrong Reject labels at its calibrated threshold 0.68 (79 at 0.90) against 47 for ConsentLens-1, for example "Cookie preferences" and "Configurar cookies". A wrong Reject on a settings button makes an audit infer a visible reject option and hides the most common consent dark pattern, so v2 is not genuinely better for TraceVeil yet (and a new file would need a fresh NPU check on the phone). The app keeps ConsentLens-1.

reproduction.statement: Seed 42 through ConsentLens-1's own training and conversion code reproduces every fold of the published metrics.json to 4 decimals (macro-F1 float and INT8, agreement, lexicon baseline).

tried_html:
Screened on the dev split (one seed each; see the table):

  • Optimisation (s1): cosine learning-rate decay, an exponential moving average of the weights (EMA 0.999), 40 epochs.
  • Regularisation (s2): byte-noise augmentation on half the rows each epoch (character drop / duplicate / swap, diacritics stripped, punctuation and spacing changes, same-class same-language concatenation for notices) plus embedding and pool dropout.
  • Capacity (s2_w160): 64-dim embedding, Conv 160×3 + Conv 160×7, Dense 160 (272 KB, 11 ops).
  • Ensembling: every pair of screened models, averaged, beat its better member on both dev splits (+0.012 to +0.056). pk2_mix_k33 packs two members into one graph: embeddings side by side, block-diagonal conv and dense kernels, last layer averages the logits; same 11 op types as v1, 389 KB.
  • Logit adjustment (foldable into the last bias): no gain on dev; the square-root class weights already balance the roles.

Built and op-checked but not screened (no laptop time left): three conv layers, dilation (written as one CONV_2D; Keras's own dilated Conv1D adds 3 new op types), stride 2. Not tried: label smoothing, focal loss, full inverse-frequency weights, language-balanced sampling, knowledge distillation. Nothing is claimed about them.

Pre-registered rule (fixed before any candidate's test numbers existed): the packed ensemble is the candidate if its dev macro-F1 is at least the best single model's on both dev splits; otherwise the best single model is. Outcome: the packed ensemble lost on the seen-language dev split (see table), so the wider single network s2_w160 is the candidate. The ensemble's outer run, started early to save time, was stopped; its two finished folds (0.646 and 0.557 vs v1's 0.574 and 0.500, seed 1, held-out languages) are incomplete and were not used for any decision.

recipe_notes.v1: ConsentLens-1 recipe (constant LR 2e-3, 30 epochs, sqrt class weights)
recipe_notes.s1: v1 network; cosine LR decay, weight EMA (0.999), 40 epochs
recipe_notes.s2: s1 + byte-noise augmentation (50% of rows per epoch) + embedding/pool dropout
recipe_notes.s2_inv: s2 with full inverse-frequency class weights
recipe_notes.s2_w160: s2, wider: 64-dim embedding, Conv 160×3 + Conv 160×7, Dense 160 (272 KB)
recipe_notes.s2_s3: s2, three conv layers with stride 2 (128/160/192)
recipe_notes.pk2_mix_k33: packed ensemble of 2 members (s1 and s2 recipes, Conv 128×3 + 128×3 each) in one graph

INT8 vs float agreement >= 98%.value: 98.9% lowest seed and protocol (lowest single fold 98.7%)

phone_checks_html:
1. AI lab → ConsentLens → Load: chip says “Running on the NPU”, logcat planNodes=1/11 fullyDelegated=true (the whole graph on the QNN HTP).
  2. Benchmark (1,000 runs): read NPU and CPU median/p95 from the card or logcat; npuCpuAgree and matchesPythonInt8 should be 24/24 or close.
  3. Try samples: the 24 phrases' roles should match the Python INT8 reference stored in consentlens_meta.json.
  4. Only after these hold, say “runs fully on the Hexagon NPU”. Until then say “built for the NPU, CPU fallback”.
